phrase: Be the change you wish to see in the world
aliases: be the change you want to see in the world
finding: Prominent misattribution to Gandhi; attribution investigations point to a 1970s modern slogan trail and a 1913 Gandhi passage as a related antecedent, not the same wording. Earliest modern hardcopy was not independently re-inspected in this corpus.

index.shortFinding: Not Gandhi. A 1913 passage of his is an antecedent, not the wording.

searchScope: Quote Investigator dossier and secondary reporting of the 1974/1987 print trail. Gandhi’s 1913 Indian Opinion passage reviewed via secondary quotation.
evidenceReviewed: QI (2017) on Lorrance 1974 trail and Gandhi 1913 antecedent; secondary reporting of 1987 Gandhi attribution.

correctionHistory.summary: Added earliest-reported 1974 modern-wording assertion and rebound the index earliest milestone from popularization to that reported occurrence.

assertions.subject: Mahatma Gandhi
assertions.publicStatement: Current evidence does not securely support coinage by Gandhi for the concise modern slogan; the polished aphorism is not traced in his writings in that form.

assertions.subject: Gandhi, Indian Opinion (1913)
assertions.publicStatement: An earlier related formulation appears in Gandhi’s 1913 writing about changing ourselves so that tendencies in the world would also change — thematically related, not the same wording.

assertions.subject: Late-1980s Gandhi attribution in U.S. press and later viral reuse
assertions.publicStatement: Popularized by later attribution to Gandhi in U.S. press (from 1987 onward in the documented trail) and subsequent viral reuse of the Gandhi credit.

assertions.subject: Arleen Lorrance, 1974 modern slogan trail
assertions.publicStatement: Attribution investigations identify a close modern slogan match in Arleen Lorrance’s 1974 writing; the primary hardcopy was not independently re-inspected in this corpus.

assertions.subject: Earliest modern slogan wording
assertions.publicStatement: The record remains incomplete for an independently re-inspected primary of the earliest modern slogan wording; attribution investigations point to Arleen Lorrance (1974), pending hardcopy re-inspection in this corpus.

sources.title: Be the Change You Wish To See in the World
sources.author: Garson O’Toole
sources.shortExcerpt: Gandhi died in 1948, and the earliest close match known to QI appeared many years later in 1974 within a book chapter written by educator Arleen Lorrance.
